topic: Early research and the first public text/video tools, 2014-2023 (video GANs to Lumiere, Jan 2024)

milestones.headline: A GAN generated tiny 64x64 clips of about a second from noise, with separate foreground and background streams, learned from unlabeled video.

specs.notes: 32 frames at 25 fps = 1.28 s (derived; paper says 'a little over a second'). Unconditional (no text prompt). NIPS 2016.

claims.claim: arXiv v1 submitted 8 Sep 2016; abstract says the model generates 'tiny videos up to a second'.
claims.quote: this model can generate tiny videos up to a second at full frame rate better than simple baselines

claims.claim: Output spec: 32 frames, 64x64, native 25 fps.
claims.quote: We extract frames at native frame rate (25 fps). We use 32-frame videos of spatial resolution 64 × 64.

milestones.notes: arXiv abs page lists 'Submitted on 8 Sep 2016 (v1), last revised 26 Oct 2016 (v3)'; abs comments: 'NIPS 2016'.

milestones.version: TGAN (Temporal Generative Adversarial Nets with Singular Value Clipping)
milestones.headline: Split video generation into a temporal generator (per-frame latent codes) and an image generator, trained stably with Wasserstein GAN plus singular value clipping.

specs.notes: Fixed length of 16 frames (per the MoCoGAN paper, which compared against it). Unconditional. Published ICCV 2017 (arXiv comment: 'to appear in ICCV 2017'); v3 revised 18 Aug 2017.

claims.claim: arXiv v1 submitted 21 Nov 2016; introduces TGAN.
claims.quote: Temporal Generative Adversarial Nets (TGAN), which can learn a semantic representation of unlabeled videos, and is capable of generating videos

claims.claim: Training data pipeline gives 16-frame, 64-pixel clips.
claims.quote: randomly extracted 16 frames, and cropped a center square with 64 pixels

claims.claim: A later paper states TGAN produces fixed 16-frame videos (VGAN 32 frames).
claims.quote: The VGAN and TGAN implementations can only generate fixed-length videos (32 frames and 16 frames correspondingly).

milestones.notes: Brief listed 'TGAN 2017': the arXiv first version is Nov 2016; the ICCV publication is 2017.

milestones.headline: Separated 'what is in the video' (content) from 'how it moves' (motion) so one subject could be given different motions.

specs.notes: Experiments used 64x64 frames and 16-frame videos; length can vary because frames are generated sequentially by a recurrent network. Unconditional/class-conditioned; no text prompts.

claims.claim: arXiv v1 submitted 17 Jul 2017; framework maps random vectors to frames.
claims.quote: The proposed framework generates a video by mapping a sequence of random vectors to a sequence of video frames.

claims.claim: Dataset spec used in experiments.
claims.quote: the image resolution was 64 × 64 and video length was 16.

milestones.notes: Brief listed 'MoCoGAN 2018': arXiv v1 is 17 Jul 2017 (v2 14 Dec 2017). The CVPR 2018 venue is commonly cited but was NOT visible in the retrieved arXiv page or PDF text, so it is not asserted here.

milestones.headline: Scaled video GANs to Kinetics-600: up to 256x256 pixels or up to 48 frames (4 s), though not both at once.

specs.notes: 256x256 and 48 frames are separate maxima: the paper compares 12-frame videos across 64/128/256 resolutions and shows 48-frame samples at 64x64. Class-conditional, no text prompts.

claims.claim: arXiv v1 submitted 15 Jul 2019; contribution statement gives resolution and length maxima.
claims.quote: produces high-quality samples at resolutions up to 256 × 256 and lengths up to 48 frames

claims.claim: Duration of the longest samples.
claims.quote: DVD-GAN is able to generate plausible videos at all resolutions and with length spanning up to 4 seconds (48 frames)

milestones.notes: Abstract on https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.06571 retrieved (Submitted 15 Jul 2019, v2 25 Sep 2019).

milestones.developer: Microsoft Research Asia and Peking University

specs.notes: Trained on ~16-frame chunks and extended block-autoregressively to 64 frames. Output fps is not stated for the samples; the paper's mention of 'at least 24 frames per second' describes typical source videos, not the model output.

specs.notes: Pipeline: 16 frames at 64x64 -> frame interpolation to 76 frames -> 256x256 -> 768x768. Fps is a conditioning input (training used random fps 1-30); the paper does not state a single output fps or duration in the text retrieved.

capabilities.capability: Text-to-video, text+image-to-video and image-to-video modes in one system
capabilities.quote: Mode 02: Text + Image to Video Generate a video using a driving image and a text prompt

capabilities.capability: Image-to-video from arbitrary starting frames (Gen-2 update before Sept 2023)
capabilities.quote: we pushed a large update to the model that allowed using arbitrary starting frames to generate videos using image-to-video

capabilities.capability: Open text-to-video diffusion model runnable by anyone (English prompts)
Animate any personalized Stable Diffusion model with a plug-in motion module, no per-model tuning
capabilities.quote: a practical framework for animating personalized T2I models without requiring model-specific tuning

capabilities.capability: Basic camera-move control via small adapters
capabilities.quote: We also support MotionLoRA of eight basic camera movements.

capabilities.capability: Sparse image/scribble conditioning of an animation
capabilities.quote: which can take abitary number of condition maps to control the animation contents

capabilities.capability: Generate and edit video in several styles (3D, anime, cartoon, cinematic)
capabilities.quote: a new AI model capable of generating and editing videos in diverse styles such as 3D animation, anime, cartoon and cinematic

capabilities.capability: Image-to-video with 14 or 25 frames at adjustable frame rate (open weights)
capabilities.quote: capable of generating 14 and 25 frames at customizable frame rates between 3 and 30 frames per second

capabilities.capability: Two-step text-to-image then image-to-video, 512x512, 4 s, 16 fps
capabilities.quote: uses just two diffusion models to generate 512x512 four-second long videos at 16 frames per second

capabilities.capability: Video and audio from one language model; portrait by default
capabilities.quote: By default, the VideoPoet model generates videos in portrait orientation to tailor its output towards short-form content.

capabilities.capability: Extend a clip by predicting the next second repeatedly (up to 10 s)
capabilities.quote: We are able to generate longer videos simply by conditioning on the last 1 second of video and predicting the next 1 second.

capabilities.capability: Whole 5-second clip generated in a single pass for global temporal consistency
capabilities.quote: a Space-Time U-Net architecture that generates the entire temporal duration of the video at once, through a single pass in the model

limitations.statement: Generating video frame by frame with an image model causes flicker and content changes between frames (the reason for dedicated video models).
limitations.quote: you’ll get a lot of flicker and changes in content between each frame

limitations.statement: SVD clips are short and not perfectly photorealistic.
limitations.quote: The generated videos are rather short (<= 4sec), and the model does not achieve perfect photorealism.

limitations.statement: SVD is not steered by text.
limitations.quote: The model cannot be controlled through text.
The model cannot render legible text.

limitations.statement: SVD faces and people can be wrong.
limitations.quote: Faces and people in general may not be generated properly.

limitations.statement: SVD may produce clips with no or little motion.
limitations.quote: The model may generate videos without motion, or very slow camera pans.
this model is not intended for real-world or commercial applications at this stage

limitations.statement: Only Chinese prompts were supported in the released code.
limitations.quote: Currently we only supports simplified Chinese input.

limitations.statement: Cannot learn text-to-motion associations that only exist in video (e.g. left-to-right vs right-to-left hand wave); longer, multi-scene stories left for future work.
limitations.quote: our approach can not learn associations between text and phenomenon that can only be inferred in videos.

limitations.statement: Web-trained models reflect and may amplify social biases.
limitations.quote: our models have learnt and likely exaggerated social biases

limitations.statement: Model withheld because of safety and bias concerns.
limitations.quote: We have decided not to release the Imagen Video model or its source code until these concerns are mitigated.

limitations.statement: Models, code, data and demo withheld.
limitations.quote: our decision not to release the underlying models, code, data or interactive demo at this time

limitations.statement: At higher resolutions coherent objects were harder to generate.
limitations.quote: At higher resolutions, generating coherent objects becomes more difficult
The performance of this model needs to be improved on complex compositional generation tasks.

limitations.statement: Not built to depict real people or events.
limitations.quote: The model was not trained to realistically represent people or events

limitations.statement: No multi-shot videos or scene transitions.
limitations.quote: our method is not designed to generate videos that consist of multiple shots, or that involve transitions between scenes.

corrections_to_common_beliefs: Make-A-Video (29 Sep 2022), Imagen Video (5 Oct 2022) and Phenaki (5 Oct 2022) were research announcements, not products. Imagen Video and Phenaki papers explicitly say the models/demos were not released; Meta's post says it only 'plan[s] to release a demo experience'.

Runway Gen-2 was announced on 2023-03-20 (first archived page capture and Runway's tweet as embedded by PetaPixel) but stayed Discord early access until general availability in June 2023; Runway's own page on Gen-2 carries a 'Feb 2023' label that does not match the first archived capture.
Runway Gen-1 (announced 2023-02-06, 'Request Access') was video-to-video, i.e. it needed a source clip; text-to-video arrived with Gen-2.

'First publicly available text-to-video' is contested: CogVideo (code, weights and web demo, May 2022) and ModelScope text-to-video (weights on Hugging Face, 2023-03-19) were public before Gen-2's June 2023 general release, though CogVideo required Chinese prompts and ModelScope was research-only, non-commercial.
Pika 1.0 was announced on 2023-11-28 with a waitlist, not released to everyone that day (Pika's launch page: 'You can join the waitlist for Pika 1.0').

Stable Video Diffusion (2023-11-21) shipped as image-to-video only (14- and 25-frame models at 576x1024, up to about 4 s), as a research preview not for commercial use; text-to-video and text control were not part of the released weights.

Early open video models are non-commercial: ModelScope (cc-by-nc-4.0; diffusers-mirror card body says CC-BY-NC-ND) and zeroscope v2 (cc-by-nc-4.0) cannot be reused in the film. AnimateDiff code is Apache-2.0 but its outputs' rights depend on the base image model used.

Deforum-style 'AI animation' was not a video model: it generated one Stable Diffusion image per frame, which is why it flickered (Runway's CTO: per-frame generation gives 'a lot of flicker and changes in content between each frame').

Early GAN/diffusion clips were tiny: VGAN 64x64 for 32 frames (~1.3 s at 25 fps); TGAN and MoCoGAN 16 frames at 64x64; DVD-GAN up to 256x256 or 48 frames (4 s) but not both; NUWA about 4 s at 2.5 fps; CogVideo 4 s at 480x480; Imagen Video's 5.3 s at 1280x768 was a paper spec, with the model withheld at announcement.
Dates on the brief: TGAN's first arXiv version is Nov 2016 (ICCV 2017 is the publication), MoCoGAN's is Jul 2017 (not 2018), and Video Diffusion Models (Apr 2022) predate CogVideo (May 2022).

VideoPoet's blog says it generates portrait video by default and can produce audio, but the audio is predicted from generated 2-second clips and the long-video mode extends by one second at a time up to about 10 s (paper).
